relations.subject: sgw:environment-variable-substitution
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (minted in configuration-overview.json, same batch) - environment variable values are read once at startup and are immutable at runtime, the same restart-dependency shape as bootstrap configuration itself
relations.evidence: The variables are immutable. This means changes to the values of the environment variables are not detected by Sync Gateway while it's running. Such changes only become effective after a restart of Sync Gateway.

notable_absence.finding: The page states 'Any references to undefined variables found in the configuration cause Sync Gateway to throw an error' - a validation/fail-fast behavior - but this was left as prose rather than forced into a relation, consistent with round 3's access-control-concepts.json which similarly left sgw:role-name-prefix-convention's 'throws if violated' behavior unmodeled as a triple. No promoted or extraction-layer predicate cleanly captures 'validation failure mode' as distinct from the settings it validates, and forcing one here for a single occurrence seemed premature.

cross_component_finding: Variable names are explicitly case-sensitive ('`${username}` and `${USERNAME}` are not the same variable'), a small but real footgun given that the same page's own Example 1 uses all-uppercase `${USERNAME}`/`${PASSWORD}` by convention with no enforcement - nothing on the page states or requires an uppercase naming convention, it is purely idiomatic in the example.
cross_product_finding: None - this page's substitution mechanism is Sync Gateway's own configuration-file feature with no analogue invoked from or to Couchbase Server or Capella in this batch.
